The record should also show that Sánchez would have been a first-year arb player in 2026 even if he hadn't signed the first of two contract extensions back in 2024. As such, he could have still been the ace for a Rays staff that doesn't have a true No. 1.

The Trade: Chicago Cubs get CF Pete Crow-Armstrong; New York Mets get SS Javier Báez, RHP Trevor Williams, cash

The Mets were seven games over .500 when they made this trade, so it's not like they were committing to some kind of quixotic playoff chase. They had a real shot at making it.

Even if it didn't pan out, Báez did his part to move the ball forward in his last few months before his first free-agency experience. His 47 games as a Met yielded a 140 OPS+ and 1.7 rWAR. Williams wasn't too shabby, either, posting a 3.06 ERA in 10 appearances.

PCA wasn't a name-brand prospect when the Cubs made this trade, but that changed in the ensuing years. Generally, what you heard about him was that he was an uncommonly good defender with amazing wheels.

Turns out he can hit, too. He went 30-30 last year despite a tendency to expand the strike zone. That tendency has largely disappeared in 2026, and he is on pace for another 30-30 campaign with a 158 OPS+. His 7.8 rWAR safely leads all MLB players.

Meanwhile, the Mets are in last place in the NL East for many reasons. It just so happens that one of MLB's worst offenses and defenses are among them.

The Trade: Tampa Bay Rays get 3B Junior Caminero; Cleveland Guardians get RHP Tobias Myers

To say that the Guardians got nothing out of Myers wouldn't be totally accurate, but it would be close.

He only made 14 appearances for their Triple-A affiliate during the 2022 season, pitching to a 6.00 ERA with 40 strikeouts against 33 walks in 60.0 innings. Come July, the Guardians sent Myers to the San Francisco Giants for cash considerations .

It is amusing in retrospect that the linked report described Caminero as a "low-level outfield prospect."

That technically was true at the time, but Caminero was a consensus top-five prospect by the time he was entering the 2024 season in the Rays' system. Cut to now, and his 80 home runs across the last two seasons are the most of any hitter in the American League.

Even if Caminero plays the same position as José Ramírez, the Guardians sure could use his bat right now. They're third from the bottom of MLB with a total of 120 home runs.

San Diego Padres: CJ Abrams and James Wood

The Trade: Washington Nationals get SS CJ Abrams, OF James Wood, LHP MacKenzie Gore, OF Robert Hassell III, 1B Luke Voit, RHP Jarlin Susana; San Diego Padres get OF Juan Soto, 1B Josh Bell

This trade was hardly a waste for the Padres. Soto was part of their playoff run in 2022, notably homering in the last two games of the National League Championship Series.

The Padres missed the playoffs in 2023, however, and they generally got the worst that Soto has to offer. His 149 OPS+ as a Padre is stellar by normal standards, yet the lowest such mark he's posted for any of the four teams he's played for.

Looking back on this trade now, the wild thing is that the Nationals' supposed centerpiece has proved to be a bust. Hassell was MLB Pipeline's No. 21 prospect at the time, but his OPS has fallen into a .500s purgatory at Triple-A.

Instead, the Nationals have gotten a total of five All-Star selections out of Gore, Abrams and Wood. Abrams and Wood are now key pieces of MLB's most prolific home run-hitting offense, combining for 59 long balls in 2026.

The Padres are doing just fine without these three, of course. Yet they'd undeniably be doing better with all three of them, perhaps to a point where they would be threatening to take down the Los Angeles Dodgers in the NL West.

The Trade: Seattle Mariners get LF Randy Arozarena; Tampa Bay Rays get RHP Brody Hopkins, OF Aidan Smith

The book on this trade is far from closed, and the Rays can't be counted out as the ultimate winner in the end. That comes down to Hopkins, who is rated by B/R's Joel Reuter as the No. 5 prospect in their system.

It's just that Hopkins' stock is, shall we say, less than ascendant. He has struck out 108 batters in 86.0 innings at the Triple-A level, but with 87 walks and a 5.34 ERA. The Rays are already testing him out as a reliever , which might be for the best.

Arozarena had a 122 OPS+ for his career as a Ray when he went to Seattle in 2024. He has since posted a 124 OPS+ as a Mariner, and that part says enough.

There's also the evolution at play with Arozarena's offense this year. He's rocking a career-high 136 OPS+, and hasn't sacrificed power (17 HR) or speed (20 SB) to make it happen. It's a heck of a salary drive ahead of his first foray into free agency.

Because he's making $15.65 million this year, it's hard to imagine any scenario in which Arozarena actually stuck with the Rays. Yet if he had, they'd be getting more than a .710 OPS and an MLB-low four home runs out of left field.

The Trade: Philadelphia Phillies get LHP Jesús Luzardo, C Paul McIntosh; Miami Marlins get INF Starlyn Caba, OF Emaarion Boyd

Caba and Boyd were both top-30 prospects in the Phillies' system at the time of this trade, and the book is far from closed on either of them. Boyd is at Double-A, while Caba has only made it as far as High-A.

Even so, neither had the helium that they once did. Only Caba ranks among Miami's top prospects , and his value is tied up in his glove. He's gotten on base at a .382 clip in the minors, but a .240 average and .325 slugging percentage hint at a bat that could be exploited by major league pitching.

Even though he had been in the big leagues for parts of six seasons, it still wasn't clear what Luzardo was supposed to be when this trade went down. He had top-of-the-rotation ability, but had struggled to put it together.

Not anymore, of course. The lefty was a down-ballot Cy Young Award contender in 2025, and now he's an All-Star with a career-best 139 ERA+ in 2026. As a result, the $135 million extension that the Phillies signed him to mere weeks before he was about to enter his walk year looks like a steal.

The Marlins have been able to stay in contention largely because of their starting pitching, but still having Luzardo obviously would have made their rotation even stronger.

The Trade: Toronto Blue Jays get RHP Louis Varland, 1B Ty France; Minnesota Twins get OF Alan Roden, LHP Kendry Rojas

This trade is barely a year old, so it's perhaps too soon to be looking at it as a failure for the Twins. It helps that both Roden and Rojas have many years to go before they exit their 20s.

Yet with 81 games under his belt, Roden only has a 58 OPS+ to show for his time in the majors. The 29.2 major league innings that Rojas has seen have yielded a solid 3.34 ERA, but also 22 walks.

To put it bluntly, this feels like the Ryan Pressly trade all over again.

Just as Pressly was a talented reliever who needed to get out of Minnesota to fully unlock his potential, the same is apparently true of Varland. He had a bit of a coming-out party in Toronto's World Series run last year, and now he's an All-Star with a 1.26 ERA and the most fWAR of any AL relief pitcher.

As for the Twins, their bullpen has the fifth-highest ERA in the league. They sure could use Varland and Jhoan Duran back now, but at least the 2025 trade that sent the latter to Philadelphia brought back a top-10 prospect in Eduardo Tait.

St. Louis Cardinals: Willson Contreras and Sonny Gray

Sonny Gray Trade (November 25, 2025): Boston Red Sox get RHP Sonny Gray, cash; St. Louis Cardinals get RHP Richard Fitts, LHP Brandon Clarke, PTBNL

Willson Contreras Trade (December 22, 2025): Boston Red Sox get 1B Willson Contreras; St. Louis Cardinals get RHP Hunter Dobbins, RHP Blake Aita, RHP Yhoiker Fajardo

Granted, these trades were not about getting talent into St. Louis' farm system. They were about cutting payroll, and they did that successfully.

Even so, these trades haven't quite proven to be loaded with pleasant surprises for the Cardinals. Maybe Fajardo, who's now one of their top-10 prospects . The only other standout so far is Dobbins, though his 50.0 innings with the big club have featured too few strikeouts (49) and too many walks (21) and home runs (7).

The short version is that the Cardinals may well have given up a real shot at contention by making these trades.

They're still hanging in the NL wild-card race at 65-62, putting them just 2.5 games off the pace for the third slot. Between this and an 11-6 surge in August, nobody should make the mistake of counting them out.

All Contreras and Gray have done in Boston, however, is emerge as the best hitter and pitcher on a team that has won 39 of its last 54 games. They've given the Red Sox real World Series aspirations that perhaps should belong to the Cardinals.

articles.title: Orioles Call for MLB Rule Change Around Foul Pole Technology After Pete Alonso's Near-HR vs. Yankees
articles.summary: The Baltimore Orioles are calling for MLB to make changes around the foul pole in the wake of a controversial call in Wednesday's loss to the New York Yankees that saw an apparent homer by Pete Alonso ruled a foul ball.
articles.body:
The Baltimore Orioles are calling for MLB to make changes around the foul pole in the wake of a controversial call in Wednesday's loss to the New York Yankees that saw an apparent homer by Pete Alonso ruled a foul ball.

Alonso appeared to hit a go-ahead solo homer in the bottom of the seventh, but the umpires called it foul and upheld the ruling after replay review even though at least one angle appeared to show the ball on the fair side of the pole.

Speaking to reporters after the game, Alonso outlined a "simple fix" in line with the pylon camera technology that the NFL uses to determine if the ball breaks the goal-line plane.

"I think a simple fix is like football, you have the pylon camera with the plane, where it shoots right across the goal line," Alonso said. "And I feel like, for us, we could easily have a laser or a camera that shoots straight up."

Orioles manager Craig Albernaz offered an idea to use ball-tracking technology that's already being used in different areas throughout MLB:

"On the dugout iPads there's ball-tracking data with the field that the players see, so it's really tough to have that [call] come back as 'stands' and have that visual in the dugout as well. It's 2026. There are teams using AI on the iPads and other sports use ball-tracking data for challengeable calls. Don't understand why we don't do it."

Alonso followed up, noting the umpires told him that MLB requires confirmation from two camera angles to overturn the original call and there was only one angle that showed clear evidence the ball was in fair territory.

"What I was told is in order to overturn a call, you need to have two camera angles to confirm it," Alonso said. "But the best view, the only view that shows the ball fair or foul is the one down the line, but no other camera angle is available. So video room rules it foul, umpire obviously called it foul initially. It is what it is."

Jacob Calvin Meyer of the Baltimore Sun shared a screenshot of one piece of tracking data that showed the ball stayed fair throughout its entire trajectory.

The score was tied 3-3 at the time of Alonso's non-homer. His at-bat ended in a strikeout that ended the seventh inning.

New York notched two runs in the top of the eighth to get a 5-3 win. The Orioles have now dropped three straight games and sit in last place in the AL East, though they are only 1.5 games out of the final wild card spot.

The Yankees and Orioles will wrap up their three-game series on Thursday at 6:35 p.m. ET.

articles.title: New Aaron Judge Injury Update Given By Aaron Boone as Yankees Star Progresses From Rib Issue
articles.summary: New York Yankees fans got a positive update on their star this week.
articles.body:
New York Yankees fans got a positive update on their star this week.

Aaron Judge, who has been sidelined since May with a rib injury, began hitting off a tee on Thursday, manager Aaron Boone said . This comes two days after Boone revealed the star would be starting his hitting progression.

The update comes after Boone said that he expects Judge to be back at some point this year, adding that he is able to play catch.

"Just part of the ramp-up to baseball activity," Boone told reporters over the weekend. "Hopefully he'll continue to progress through this week. We'll see what else gets introduced. ... We expect him back, but we're in the early stages of baseball activity."

Judge last played on May 31 and landed on the injured list after tests showed a stress fracture in one of his ribs. While the Yankees initially estimated he'd be back on the field in four to six weeks, but its now been months.

Judge hadn't exactly been playing his best baseball before the injury, as he had a .248/.375/.533 slash line along with 17 home runs and 38 RBI in 59 games. If he's able to return this year, the Yankees hope to get him back into his MVP form.

Along with the update on Judge, Boone offered some insight into where the team is with Max Fried. The reliever was placed on the 15-day injured list with a bone bruise in his pitching elbow, but Boone described it as a precautionary measure.

"We just kind of collectively decided it's probably best to make sure we get this calmed down," he told reporters . "Hopefully, keep it a smaller issue, which is the hope."

Fried also missed two months earlier this season with the same injury.

New York has battled injuries throughout the season but is still sitting in second place in the AL East at 69-55 and currently is 8.5 games ahead in the wild-card race with just over a month remaining in the regular season.

articles.title: Kade Anderson Reportedly Called Up By Mariners, MLB's No. 1 Pitching Prospect
articles.summary: The Seattle Mariners plan to call up top pitching prospect Kade Anderson, according to ESPN's Jeff Passan.
articles.body:
The Seattle Mariners plan to call up top pitching prospect Kade Anderson, according to ESPN's Jeff Passan .

Anderson is expected to start against the Chicago Cubs on Saturday after getting called up, per Passan.

Expectations are high for the left-hander, as he's listed as the No. 1 pitching prospect as well as the No. 5 overall prospect among all teams (via MLB.com ).

Seattle selected Anderson with the No. 3 overall pick in the 2025 MLB draft.

He suited up for LSU from 2024-25 before spending time with Double-A Arkansas to open the 2026 season.

Anderson has been dominant in the minor leagues this year, owning a 10-1 record in 18 starts while ranking No. 1 among all Texas League pitchers with his 1.06 ERA and 0.643 WHIP.

He's also racked up 135 strikeouts compared to a mere 13 walks in 93.1 innings of work. Opposing batters are hitting just .147 against him.

Anderson will immediately step into a rotation role with Seattle, as Mariners president of baseball operations Jerry Dipoto previously confirmed that he wouldn't be used in a bullpen role in the majors.

"We're not going to put Kade in the bullpen," Dipoto said on Aug. 4, per MLB.com's Daniel Kramer . "He's the best starting pitcher in the minor leagues. I think he leads the minor leagues in everything, not [just] the Texas League, but [all of] the minor leagues. And he is trending in every way you can."

The Mariners' starting pitching has been a strength this season, ranking No. 7 among all MLB teams with a combined ERA of 3.89.

Still, Seattle only holds the No. 3 spot in the American League West standings with a 60-68 record. The Mariners sit 4.5 games back from the division lead and three games back from the final AL Wild Card spot.

As they attempt to clinch consecutive postseason appearances for the first time since 1999, Anderson will be in the mix.

articles.title: Rangers' Jacob deGrom Makes MLB History with 2,000 Career Strikeouts
articles.summary: Jacob deGrom reached an impressive individual milestone during the Texas Rangers' clash with the Washington Nationals on Thursday night.
articles.body:
Jacob deGrom reached an impressive individual milestone during the Texas Rangers' clash with the Washington Nationals on Thursday night.

The two-time Cy Young Award winner recorded his 2,000th career strikeout in the first inning of the game.

He also amassed 2,000 strikeouts in the fewest total innings pitched by a right-hander in MLB history.

With deGrom's latest accomplishment, he became the 94th pitcher to rack up at least 2,000 strikeouts (h/t ESPN ). He's also the fourth player to reach the threshold this season, joining Kevin Gausman, Sonny Gray and Aaron Nola.

Joining the 2,000-strikeout club is a particularly impressive achievement for deGrom considering the injuries that have taken a toll on his career.

He was limited to just 35 total starts from 2021-24, navigating through a scapular stress reaction in 2022 before undergoing Tommy John surgery in 2023. It marked the second Tommy John procedure of his career, as he previously underwent the same surgery in 2010.

Still, deGrom came back and put together an impressive 2025 season in which he earned an All-Star nod and finished No. 8 in American League Cy Young award voting .

This year, the five-time All-Star owned an 8-8 record in 23 starts heading into Thursday's action. He's compiled a 3.95 ERA while limiting opposing hitters to a .237/.284/.391 slash line.

Now, deGrom is looking to end his 2026 campaign on a high note and help the Rangers reach the postseason for the first time since their World Series victory in 2023.

Texas currently sits at No. 2 in the AL West standings with a 62-65 record. The Rangers are 0.5 games back from the final Wild Card spot and two games back from the division lead.

articles.title: The MLB Awards Race Dividing Baseball Fans
articles.summary: Shohei Ohtani vs. Pete Crow-Armstrong for NL MVP? Whatever. That's a rookie debate, not to be confused with the rookie debate in baseball right now.
articles.body:
Shohei Ohtani vs. Pete Crow-Armstrong for NL MVP? Whatever. That's a rookie debate, not to be confused with the rookie debate in baseball right now.

Who is the National League Rookie of the Year? Is it JJ Wetherholt? Or is it Sal Stewart?

Fans of the St. Louis Cardinals and Cincinnati Reds won't be able to check their biases on this one. They have their reasons, and the problem for the rest of us is how those reasons combine to form one impossible-to-solve puzzle.

Simply trying to put it together reveals something about the state of baseball discourse—specifically, that how players are valued might be changing.

So, strap in as we break down the debate that's breaking baseball.

JJ Wetherholt vs. Sal Stewart for NL Rookie of the Year, Briefly Explained

In the Redbirds' corner is Wetherholt, a slick-fielding second baseman who also wields a solid stick. In the Reds' corner is Stewart, a first baseman with a less interesting glove but a mightier stick.

It's an interesting awards battle just based on that sales pitch, and FanDuel's current odds indeed portray this as a two-horse race:

However, there's a Wins Above Replacement twist at play. Any direct consultation with WAR will tell you this race should not be close between Wetherholt and Stewart:

So you're telling me that Wetherholt is more than twice as valuable as Stewart? If that's the case, what are we even doing here?

That's Cardinals fans talking, and they might as well be gesturing at Wetherholt's defense and baserunning. His defense, especially, isn't merely strong. It's exceptional. He's in the top 10 among all fielders with +14 Defensive Runs Saved, and in the top three with +22 Outs Above Average.

As a defender, Stewart pretty much breaks even at first base and third base. Reds fans might counter that his versatility (i.e., 300-plus innings at both spots) matters, though not nearly as much as his offense.

Stewart has 11 more home runs (27 to 16) and 50 RBI (96 to 46) on Wetherholt. Stewart's OPS is also 88 points higher, at .809 to .721, something that can't be yada-yada'd away as a benefit of Great American Ball Park. It's hitter-friendly, but not that hitter-friendly.

Echoes of the Awards Debate That Changed Everything

At the risk of making a dated reference, the Wetherholt vs. Stewart debate feels like a throwback to Miguel Cabrera vs. Mike Trout for the American League MVP in 2012.

Per the usual MVP standards, Cabrera should have won in a rout. He won the Triple Crown by batting .330 with 44 home runs and 139 RBI—a feat not seen in MLB since 1967. It has not been accomplished again since, though Yordan Alvarez of the Houston Astros is trying to change that.

When the ballots were counted, though, Cabrera only received 22 out of 28 first-place votes.

This was WAR announcing itself as a new force to be reckoned with . For all of Cabrera's trad-stat might, his 7.1 WAR looked way up at Trout's 10.5 WAR.

Trout's case wasn't even a hard sell, as a player with a .326 average, 30 homers and 49 stolen bases to go with sensational center field defense was clearly valuable. Maybe, just maybe , even more valuable than a Triple Crown winner.

WAR clearly lost that battle, but it has since won the war. Specifically with MVP races, the correlation between WAR and voting has become too strong to deny . It's to a point where a WAR edge can trump anything else, even something as astounding as a 60-homer season by a catcher.

What Makes Wetherholt vs. Stewart Feel Different

As much as the new wisdom suggests Wetherholt should be running away with the NL Rookie of the Year, it's remarkable that it doesn't feel that way. It's as if the division between Cardinals and Reds fans has broken containment.

More than the odds, the vibe of the Wetherholt vs. Stewart race is captured in MLB.com's most recent Rookie of the Year poll. The two are tied in total points, with Wetherholt earning just two more first-place votes than Stewart.

The takeaway is not that WAR has lost its grip. If it is weakening, though, a couple of theories for why come to mind.

Award races achieve maximum fun when there's a good debate to be had. WAR doesn't make this altogether impossible—see Aaron Judge vs. Jose Altuve in 2017—but its ascension has essentially turned the stat into a Magic 8-Ball. What does the WAR Ball say? Just shake it and there's your answer.

Useful? Sure. But a tired act? Maybe that, too.

Theory 2: People Just Like a Good Hitter

More to the point, maybe what people really like is a young hitter who's so much better than a young hitter has any right to be.

Stewart is only 22 years old, so to see him with 27 bombs and 96 ribbies is impressive. That particularly goes for the ribbies, as Sarah Langs of MLB.com notes that Stewart is on track to become only the third rookie to lead his league in RBI.

There's also something about a good hitter that (pardon the expression) hits different in 2026. Nearly half of all four-seam fastballs are 95 mph. A quarter of all swings are whiffs. The league is batting .244. If a hitter can make it in this league, he deserves an award.

This is a Pepsi Challenge if there ever was one, and the head and the heart reach different conclusions.

The head prefers Wetherholt, obviously. Just look at all that WAR! Even if it has a lot to do with his defense, it's not misleading. The metrics confirm what the eye test sees: a talented shortstop who is overqualified as a second baseman.

The heart, on the other hand, prefers Stewart. There will never not be something magnetic about a guy who goes out and rakes, and all those RBI come from a place of genuine comfort in the clutch. His OPS is over 1.000 with runners in scoring position and in high-leverage spots.

Context matters, too. The Reds only have 499 RBI as a team this season. Stewart is one guy on the team, yet he's responsible for 19.2 percent of those. Bonkers.

None of this is theoretical. It's just fact. That gives it a sort of shiny-object appeal over Wetherholt's defense-first profile. Metrics like DRS and OAA ultimately represent a best guess at a player's quality in the field. You have to trust that he's saved so many more outs and so many more runs than the average second baseman. By extension, you have to trust that WAR is right.

Granted, the odds of the NL Rookie of the Year voters boarding that trust train remain high. Yet if this becomes another example of WAR winning the day, the question of why awards races need voters will only become more salient.

Stats courtesy of Baseball Reference , FanGraphs and Baseball Savant .

articles.title: Predicting Each MLB Team's Face of the Franchise in 2029
articles.summary: Which player will be the face of every MLB franchise three years from now?
articles.body:
Which player will be the face of every MLB franchise three years from now?

Except for the NL West, all the division races are within five games, and the seven-car pile-up that is the battle for the last wild-card spot in the American League all but guarantees to come right down to the wire.

But we've still got at least another few weeks before those postseason races become daily must-watch theatre. That's why mid-August has always been a prime window for gazing into cloudy crystal balls with topics like this one.

Ahead, we've identified the player we expect to be "the guy" for each team in 2029, based on a combination of age, contract status, prospect potential and more. On the off-chance we're wrong, we're also including a "Don't Sleep On" player for each team who could become the face of the franchise.

Of note, there are a few big-time impending free agents worth considering here.

Tarik Skubal hits the open market for the first time this winter. Munetaka Murakami, Adley Rutschman and Jeremy Peña headline a solid class of guys who could become very rich next offseason. And then you've got Gunnar Henderson, Ronald Acuña Jr., CJ Abrams and plenty more slated for free agency after 2028.

We won't be projecting landing spots for any of those players here, but we know they could become the singular star of wherever they land.

AL Central | AL East | AL West | NL Central | NL East | NL West

Baltimore Orioles : 1B Pete Alonso (signed through 2030)

With any luck, the O's will be able to re-up with Gunnar Henderson before he hits free agency for the first time in 2028. But, if not, at least we know the Polar Bear isn't going anywhere any time soon. He'll be 34 by the time the 2029 season begins, but there's a decent chance he'll cross the "400 career home runs" threshold during that campaign.

Boston Red Sox : OF Roman Anthony (signed through at least 2033)

It has been a disappointing 2026 campaign for Anthony, who has been out since early May with a torn tendon in his ring finger. (He did finally start a rehab assignment on Tuesday, though.) But the Red Sox surely still have grand plans for the star outfielder who signed an eight-year, $130M extension shortly after his arrival in the bigs last summer.

New York Yankees : OF Aaron Judge (signed through 2031)

The Yankees also have Max Fried signed through 2032, Cam Schlittler under team control through 2031 and George Lombard Jr. just a few weeks into what could be a marvelous career. But, come on. "All Rise" is going to be the face of this franchise until he retires, much like Derek Jeter before him. He'll turn 37 early on in the 2029 season and, injuries permitting, should reach 500 career home runs not long after.

Tampa Bay Rays : 3B Junior Caminero (under team control through 2030)

Caminero hit 45 home runs last year in his age-21 campaign, and he's on pace for an identical total this year. Even if he 'only' gets to 41, he would be the first player in MLB history with two seasons of 41 or more home runs before his age-23 year. Do you suppose Cleveland regrets trading him for Tobias Myers yet?

Toronto Blue Jays : 1B Vladimir Guerrero Jr. (signed through 2039)

He darn well better be the face of the franchise in 2029, right? The latter years of Guerrero's 14-year, $500M megadeal might be a bit painful for the Blue Jays, but he will have just turned 30 at the start of 2029 and should still be in his prime, ideally leaving this disappointing 2026 season well behind him in the rearview mirror.

Chicago White Sox : SS Colson Montgomery (under team control through 2031)

Munetaka Murakami only signed a two-year deal with the White Sox this past winter, so he isn't a candidate here. It's really a tossup between the other two sluggers in this lineup: Colson Montgomery and Miguel Vargas. And though there's a chance that 2026 No. 1 overall pick Roch Cholowsky will be making a real impact by 2029, we'll take the current shortstop who also clubbed 21 home runs in just 71 games played last season.

Cleveland Guardians : 3B José Ramírez (signed through 2032)

If it ain't broke, don't fix it. And with Ramírez re-upping on a seven-year extension this past winter, he's pretty well locked in as the face of this franchise through at least the end of the decade. He's arguably already one of the players on Cleveland's Mount Rushmore, and he's probably going to go down as the greatest player in this franchise's history when all is said and done.

Detroit Tigers : SS Kevin McGonigle (signed through 2034)

When the Tigers signed McGonigle to an eight-year, $150M extension a whole three weeks into his MLB career, it was a calculated risk. Already, though, it's looking like it could be a preposterously team-friendly contract. He's going to win AL Rookie of the Year and may well finish in the top five of AL MVP voting. He and Max Clark are going to be quite the infield/outfield tandem for years to come.

Kansas City Royals : SS Bobby Witt Jr. (signed through at least 2030)

Since his arrival in 2022, Witt has amassed 120 home runs, 181 stolen bases, an .841 OPS, a pair of Gold Gloves and a batting crown. Save for three-time MVP Aaron Judge and four-time MVP Shohei Ohtani, he has been the most valuable player of the past half-decade. Even if he opts out of the remainder of his contract after 2030, it's likely he would do so as the second-greatest Royal ever, behind only George Brett.

Minnesota Twins : OF Walker Jenkins (has not yet made MLB debut)

Joe Ryan has one year left before he hits free agency. Both Byron Buxton and Royce Lewis will also be hitting the open market after 2028. So unless you're all-in on Brooks Lee or Luke Keaschall becoming stars, it's tough to identify an active Twin who is destined for greatness. They do have a highly touted prospect in Walker Jenkins, though, who has been raking at Triple-A thus far in August. He could be a crucial September call-up and a key piece of this core as early as next season.

Athletics : 1B Nick Kurtz (under team control through 2031)

Kurtz is not one of the four hitters that the A's have managed to sign to an early contract extension, but he also isn't going to reach free agency any time soon. Through his first 204 games in the majors, he clubbed 56 home runs with 152 RBI. And if he can even remotely replicate that for the foreseeable future, the only question is who becomes the other half of Bash Brothers 2.0?

Houston Astros : OF Cam Smith (under team control through 2030)

Of the 17 Astros who have recorded either 230 plate appearances or 55 innings pitched this season, only four are controllable through 2029. Of that quartet, only Cam Smith can reasonably be considered a long-term building block—and even that is questionable. On top of that, the Astros have arguably the least promising farm system among the 30 teams. The outlook could change, but Houston could also be in a bleak position three years from now.

Los Angeles Angels : OF Mike Trout (signed through 2030)

Trout will turn 38 during the 2029 campaign, but can you come up with a better candidate here? Even if they keep both Zach Neto and Nolan Schanuel for as long as they can, both of those former first-round picks will be hitting free agency after 2029 (if they don't sign extensions first). And Trout has been more valuable than both of them this season anyway. He's also currently at 424 home runs and reasonably could get to 500 in 2029.

Seattle Mariners : CF Julio Rodríguez (signed through at least 2029)

After the 2028 season, the Mariners have to decide if they're going to exercise an eight-year club option of at least $240M for 2030-37. If they decline it, he can exercise a five-year, $90M player option for 2030-34. But 2029 would be really awkward if the M's go that route. If they pick up the option, though—which, if they had to decide today, they probably would—they're locking him in as their main man for well into the 2030s.

Texas Rangers : SS Corey Seager (signed through 2031)

Seager will turn 35 early in the 2029 campaign, which is a tough ask for a shortstop who has already endured more than his fair share of injuries over the past nine years. But if not Seager, then whom? An even older Brandon Nimmo? Evan Carter or Wyatt Langford in what presently would be his final year before free agency? Maybe their 20-year-old top prospect will be ready to shine by then, but we'll go with the $325M Seager for now.

Atlanta Braves : CF Michael Harris II (signed through at least 2030)

In addition to our official "Don't Sleep On" pick of Drake Baldwin, don't sleep on Matt Olson becoming an inescapable narrative in 2029. If he continues to play in every game—and if there actually are 162 games played in 2027—he's on track to reach third place behind only Cal Ripken Jr. and Lou Gehrig on MLB's consecutive games played list in early May 2029. But Harris' eight-year, $72M contract (with club options for 2031 and 2032) is the gift that keeps on giving to Atlanta.

Miami Marlins : OF Owen Caissie (under team control through 2031)

The year 2029 could be a make-or-break one for the Marlins, with Otto Lopez, Xavier Edwards, Kyle Stowers, Max Meyer and Eury Pérez all slated to hit free agency that winter. But considering they gave up three years of team control of Edward Cabrera to get Owen Caissie (and two other prospects) this past offseason, they've got to be hoping he'll become a major piece of the puzzle.

New York Mets : OF Juan Soto (signed through at least 2029)

Soto could opt out of the 10 years and $460M left on his contract after 2029, but the Mets could also void the opt out by turning it into a 10-year, $500M deal from that point forward. So, he's probably a Met for life at this point, and they didn't give him $765M in December 2024 for him to not be the face of this franchise in 2029.

Philadelphia Phillies : LHP Cristopher Sánchez (signed through 2031)

The Phillies have six players signed through at least 2030, but four of them—Bryce Harper, Kyle Schwarber, Trea Turner and Aaron Nola—will be in their age-36 season in 2029. Maybe Harper or Schwarber will still be the star of the show at this point, but let's finally get a pitcher onto the list, yeah? And outside of maybe Tarik Skubal, Cristopher Sánchez has been the best pitcher in baseball since the beginning of last season. His six-year, $104M contract sure is looking like a steal these days.

Washington Nationals : OF James Wood (under team control through 2030)

Had he not landed on the IL with an oblique strain in early August, there was a real chance Wood was going to get to 45 home runs, 100 RBI and 25 stolen bases. That's a line that has been achieved just six times in MLB history, and only by Shohei Othani (twice) in the past 25 years. Not too shabby for a 23-year-old who has also drawn 90 walks this season.

Chicago Cubs : CF Pete Crow-Armstrong (signed through 2032)

Pete Crow-Armstrong vs. Shohei Ohtani for NL MVP has become quite the heated debate, but there's no debating who the face of the Cubs is. They locked in PCA on a six-year, $115M extension just a few days before this season began, meaning he'll cost them, on average, less than $20M per year through 2032. What a steal for a guy who might mess around and join the 40/40 club while winning a Platinum Glove.

Cincinnati Reds : 1B/3B Sal Stewart (under team control through 2031)

2029 is going to be Cincinnati's last year of control on Elly De La Cruz. And given Scott Boras' history of not letting his guys sign extensions before hitting free agency, that isn't likely to change. So there's a good chance Stewart will be the guy for the Reds by three years from now—if he isn't already. With 27 home runs and an MLB-best 96 RBI, he's in a two-horse race with JJ Wetherholt for NL Rookie of the Year.

Milwaukee Brewers : RHP Jacob Misiorowski (under team control through 2031)

Jackson Chourio, Cooper Pratt and No. 1 overall prospect Jesús Made could all be the correct answer here, as position players naturally have a leg up on pitchers in face of the franchise conversations. But Misiorowski isn't just another pitcher. He is a weekly spectacle, 80 percent of the way through arguably the most dominant pitching season in at least a quarter century. If he can stay healthy, he's going to have multiple Cy Youngs by 2029 and will be " the Brewer" much like Clayton Kershaw was " the Dodger" for a while.

Pittsburgh Pirates : SS Konnor Griffin (signed through 2034)

Like De La Cruz in Cincinnati, Paul Skenes is the current face of the franchise in Pittsburgh. However, it feels like a sure thing that 2029 will also be his final season with the Pirates—if they even keep him that long. But Griffin entered 2026 as arguably the top prospect in all of baseball, and his legacy in the Steel City is just getting started. It's a shame that injuries have limited him to just eight games played since the end of May, but he is already a star in the making.

St. Louis Cardinals : IF JJ Wetherholt (signed through 2034)

Joshua Báez made a historic one-game first impression with three home runs in his MLB debut last week, but Wetherholt has made the best full-season first impression in St. Louis since Albert Pujols won Rookie of the Year in 2001. He is the biggest reason the Cardinals have a tangible postseason pulse right now, and they've already locked him in for the next eight years for barely $14M a pop.

Arizona Diamondbacks : OF Corbin Carroll (signed through at least 2030)

Carroll just turned 26 on Friday, yet he is already MLB's active leader in career triples with 58. There's a chance he'll end up with 20 triples, 20 home runs and 20 stolen bases this season, which hasn't been done since 2007. And he's still just getting started. Wherever the Snakes go from here, he is the foundation.

Colorado Rockies : 1B T.J. Rumfield (under team control through 2031)

The only player for the Rockies with a known salary in 2029 is Ezequiel Tovar, and he simply has not been the same player since they inked him to a seven-year, $63.5M extension in 2024. But maybe Rumfield becomes the building block this franchise has been looking for since running off Nolan Arenado and Trevor Story. They got Rumfield from the Yankees in January for the low price of Angel Chivilli, and he has quickly become their co-MVP alongside Hunter Goodman, whose last year of arbitration eligibility will be in 2029.

Los Angeles Dodgers : DH/RHP Shohei Ohtani (signed through 2033)

Whether he'll still be pitching in 2029 remains to be seen, but the four-time MVP is the face of Major League Baseball right now. It's hard to imagine he will not still be the face of the Dodgers in 2029, when he will be in his age-34 season with four years remaining on his $700M contract. Heck, 2029 could even be when he passes Barry Bonds for most MVP trophies in a career. (Though, we shall see if he can edge out PCA for No. 5 this year.)

San Diego Padres : RF Fernando Tatis Jr. (signed through 2034)

Two months into this season, Tatis' 14-year contract was starting to look like more of a curse than a gift. But after posting a .595 OPS through his first 50 games, he has been north of .900 over the past 76 contests, mashing his own home runs when not busy robbing others' grand slams. He might already be the greatest Padre not named Tony Gwynn or Trevor Hoffman, and it probably won't be long before he leaves Hoffman in the dust.

San Francisco Giants : 1B/DH Bryce Eldridge (under team control through 2031)

The Giants will still be paying Rafael Devers, Matt Chapman and Willy Adames a ton of money through 2029 and beyond, but it rather feels like "Bryce Eldridge or bust" as far as a face of the franchise is concerned. Maybe Devers flips that script and wins back over the fans, but this rookie already looks the part in his age-21 campaign.

articles.title: Little League World Series 2026 Friday Scores, Bracket Results and Highlights
articles.summary: The 2026 Little League World Series continued Friday with a loaded slate after rain delays pushed back a handful of games.
articles.body:
The 2026 Little League World Series continued Friday with a loaded slate after rain delays pushed back a handful of games.

That meant there were eight games on schedule with four international matches and four between American teams.

Here is a look at the full schedule and results. The bracket can be found in full on the Little League World Series website .

Little League World Series 2026 Monday Schedule, TV Info and Bracket Predictions

Mountain (Nevada) def. Great Lakes (Ohio), 6-5

Midwest (Iowa) def. West (California), 1-0

Northwest (Washington) def. Southwest (Texas), 4-3

Metro (New Jersey) def. Mid-Atlantic (Pennsylvania), 3-1

Mexico wasted no time pushing three runs across the board in the first inning and never looked back on the way to a commanding 7-1 victory over Australia.

Jorge Fonseca led the way with three runs scored, while Gareth Garcia notched two RBI. Mexico also used plenty of small ball to generate the runs and capitalized on its opportunities.

Fonseca did more than just score offensively.

He also struck out six and allowed just two hits in three shutout innings on the mound. From there, Esteban Bautista and Paul Lavenant combined to allow just one run in the final three innings.

The day's first real dramatics came in Nevada's 6-5 victory over Ohio.

Both teams battled back and forth throughout the game, but Nevada had the last chance at the plate. And it took full advantage when Hudson Cowley delivered a walk-off single to play the role of hero.

Ohio built a 2-0 lead and then a 5-2 advantage, but Nevada continued to battle back. The victors scored two runs in the bottom of the fourth, another in the bottom of the fifth and the winner in the sixth.

Maddox Bryan also played well with two hits and two RBI before Cowley ended things with his hit.

Iowa didn't just defeat California 1-0 in Friday's matchup.

Cooper Thissen did much of the heavy lifting in the combined no-hitter with 15 strikeouts in 5.1 innings of work. However, Anthony Johnson Jr. had to finish the job and did so in clutch fashion with a bases-loaded strikeout to end the game and preserve the 1-0 advantage.

Pitching like that would have been enough to make Thissen the hero, but he also delivered a solo homer in the first inning for the game's only run.

It was a Shohei Ohtani-like performance from the two-way star, and Iowa came away with the win as a result.

The combined no-hitters weren't limited to the United States side of the bracket.

Curaçao defeated Japan 6-0 and didn't allow a single hit in the process. Jaymiell Martina started things by striking out seven in 4.2 innings of work, while Giendry Ryan struck out four in the final 1.1 innings to put the finishing touches on the masterpiece.

Curaçao didn't need much offense with the pitching brilliance leading the way, but it got plenty on the way to six runs.

Steven Felix notched two RBI, while Raymiel Antonia went 2-for-2 with a run scored.

It would have been difficult to script a more dramatic finish to Washington's 4-3 victory over Texas than what unfolded Friday.

It seemed as if Texas was going to win with some late-game heroics when it loaded the bases with nobody out in the bottom half of the sixth inning, but pitcher Kasen Workman escaped the jam by inducing two groundouts and a fly out to secure the win.

Paxton Hansen also pitched a shutout inning in relief for Washington, which helped it preserve its early advantage.

Workman made an impact offensively with two RBI as well, while Winston Weaver and Evan Yarbrough each notched an RBI as well.

Nicaragua's 6-4 victory over Panama marked yet another game that came down to the final batter in Friday's slate.

First, Nicaragua scored four runs in the top half of the sixth inning to take the 6-3 lead. However, Panama pushed a run across in the bottom half of the frame and had the bases loaded before Nicaragua won it with a play at the plate on a wild pitch.

Kendry Arauz Roque drove in two runs with the bat and pitched the first 3.2 innings for the victors, while Moises Estrada Juarez allowed just one run in two innings.

Lucas Olmos and Jadhier Rivera each had two hits for Panama, but it wasn't enough to overcome the final deficit.

New Jersey took an early lead and never relinquished it during a 3-1 victory over Pennsylvania.

In the bottom of the second inning, New Jersey gained a 2-0 advantage after Jett Bridges scored on a wild pitch and Joey Dwyer drove in AJ Tapia with a single.

New Jersey struck again in the bottom of the fourth, as Mason Rincon hit a solo home run to right field.

Pennsylvania finally responded once Dillon DiGiulio scored on an error in the fifth inning. The team also had runners at second and third in the same frame, but couldn't drive them in.

New Jersey ultimately held on for the win, as Chase Klimkowski pitched 5.1 innings without allowing an earned run. Klimkowski also recorded six strikeouts.

Led by a dominant pitching performance, Korea took down Czechia in the final matchup of the day.

Both teams were tied 0-0 through two innings of action, although Korea took a 1-0 lead in the top of the third.

After Ki Hyun Jung opened the inning with a single and advanced to second on an error, he stole third and scored on a wild pitch to give his team an early advantage.

Another error allowed Ju Won Kim to score in the top of the fifth inning before Korea added three insurance runs in the sixth, highlighted by a two-run homer from Hyun Been Han.

Do Yoon Kim, Ha Jun Ju and Ji Hwan Hong combined to allow just one hit in six scoreless innings of work while racking up 11 total strikeouts.

articles.title: New Vladimir Guerrero Jr. Injury Update Reveals Blue Jays Star's Return Timeline After Concussion
articles.summary: Toronto Blue Jays star Vladimir Guerrero Jr. is on track to return Saturday from the concussion that has sidelined him since Aug. 14.
articles.body:
Toronto Blue Jays star Vladimir Guerrero Jr. is on track to return Saturday from the concussion that has sidelined him since Aug. 14.

Guerrero passed his final concussion tests and is "feeling good today," Blue Jays manager John Schneider told reporters Friday (h/t MLB.com's Keegan Matheson and broadcaster Hazel Mae ).

Schneider said Guerrero is expected to hit in cages Friday before returning to the lineup the following day, per Mae.

The second game of the Blue Jays' weekend series against the New York Yankees is scheduled for 1:35 p.m. ET Saturday in the Bronx.

Guerrero underwent concussion testing after his head took contact from the knee of Yankees shortstop George Lombard Jr. in a collision at third base on Aug. 14.

He was placed on the seven-day concussion injured list the following day, making Saturday the first day he will be eligible for return.

Guerrero took the first step toward a return by serving as DH for Single-A Dunedin Thursday night.

He went 1-for-1 with an RBI double and drew two walks before he was removed from the game in the fourth inning.

Guerrero has batted .263 with seven home runs through 115 games to mark his least productive campaign since 2020.

The Blue Jays have gone 3-2 since Guerrero's concussion as Alejandro Kirk took over Guerrero's usual spot in the three hole while rookie Charles McAdoo has been productive throughout the lineup.

"We're going to continue to be a team that's built around him, and however he fits in, he's going to understand," Schneider said about where Guerrero would slot back into the lineup in a Friday appearance on Sportsnet 590 The Fan . "It's not gonna hurt his feelings if he's hitting second or if he's hitting third. He gets it. He's watching how we're playing."

Whether the Blue Jays are able to build on their momentum while slotting Guerrero back into the lineup could be key to the club's playoff hopes. Toronto is heading into the weekend series against the Yankees half a game back of both the Minnesota Twins and Texas Rangers for the final Wild Card spot in the AL.

articles.title: Rafael Devers Says He's 'Matured' Since Red Sox Trade, Talks Return to Fenway Park with Giants
articles.summary: Rafael Devers feels he has matured since being traded last June to the San Francisco Giants from the Boston Red Sox.
articles.body:
Rafael Devers feels he has matured since being traded last June to the San Francisco Giants from the Boston Red Sox.

"I feel really good. I think it's been a year. I think I have matured during that year," Devers said via an interpreter when asked Friday how he had changed since the trade (h/t WEEI's Rob Bradford).

"I think that I have learned as an athlete there are things that are going to happen, and what you have to do is just move forward and learn from that."

Devers' comments came shortly before he stepped up for his first Fenway at-bat since being traded to San Francisco.

He was met by a mix of cheers and boos before he struck out looking on his fourth pitch of the game.

"I don't want to think about the past, I don't want to talk about the past," Devers said via interpreter about the emotions surrounding his return.

"But at the same time, we're all men, we're all grown-ups. We have to understand this is the business of baseball. But at the same time, you make mistakes, and you have to move on and mature."

Devers won the 2018 World Series with the Red Sox and signed an 11-year extension with the club in 2023 before his relationship with the club began to dissolve last season.

The Red Sox signed third baseman Alex Bregman ahead of the 2025 campaign, sparking disagreement when the club moved Devers to designated hitter. Devers later refused to move again when injuries opened up a spot at first base.

Red Sox president and CEO Sam Kennedy later said the club had reached an "inflection point" in its relationship with Devers before trading him to the Giants.

When asked Friday if he would change anything about how his tenure in Boston ended, Devers answered, "No."

Devers has slashed .244/.320/.470 with 25 home runs in his first full season with the Giants, which are a long shot to make the postseason after a 52-75 start to the season.

When asked Friday if he ever considered the possibility of coming back to Boston, Devers' interpreter said he sees that as a decision out of his control and is focused on his current tenure with San Francisco.

articles.title: Torey Lovullo Felt 'Betrayed' After Ketel Marte's Absence, Talks Relationship with D-Backs Star
articles.summary: Arizona Diamondbacks manager Torey Lovullo said he felt "betrayed" when second baseman Ketel Marte did not show up to a Monday game at the Boston Red Sox.
articles.body:
Arizona Diamondbacks manager Torey Lovullo said he felt "betrayed" when second baseman Ketel Marte did not show up to a Monday game at the Boston Red Sox.

"Once I saw what was unfolding, I became extremely frustrated. I felt betrayed," Lovullo told reporters Friday about his reaction to Marte's absence. "And that's a whole different type of pain and frustration. But I'm through that."

When asked what caused Marte's no-show, Lovullo said he thought there was "maybe a little bit of frustration" built around his left knee injury.

Little League World Series star Kinley Rasmus' MLB family

"I think he got tired, he got frustrated by a few things that I want to keep personal, and we're going to work through that," Lovullo said.

The Diamondbacks originally announced Monday that Marte had been placed on the restricted list before the road game against the Red Sox.

MLB.com's Steve Gilbert reported the move was made because Marte had not arrived despite the Diamondbacks hoping "up until close to game time" he would be there.

The Arizona Republic 's Nick Piecoro reported the following day Marte was returning to Arizona in order to undergo an MRI on his knee.

Marte and his agent met Thursday about the incident with Lovullo and Arizona general manager Mike Hazen, per Gilbert .

Both Hazen and Lovullo said afterward they felt the conversation was "productive."

"We covered a lot of ground. We were able to say things that we needed to say to one another, and we are going to turn the page as quickly as possible and get Ketel back in a healthy frame of mind from a physical standpoint," Lovullo said.

Lovullo concluded, "I think the conclusion that was drawn up yesterday is that we could have been better, and Ketel could have been better, specifically, and admittedly so."

Lovullo added of his relationship with Marte: "I love Ketel Marte — my relationship with him is not going to change."

Marte will begin rehabbing in Scottsdale starting Friday. Lovullo said the Diamondbacks are hoping to get him back by the time he's eligible to return from the 10-day injured list as the Diamondbacks continue fighting for an NL Wild Card spot down the stretch.

articles.title: Ranking Every MLB Team's 2026 Home Run Leader from Obvious to Shocking
articles.summary: It should come as a surprise to no one to look at the MLB leaderboards and see guys like Kyle Schwarber and Shohei Ohtani leading their respective teams in home runs once again this year.
articles.body:
It should come as a surprise to no one to look at the MLB leaderboards and see guys like Kyle Schwarber and Shohei Ohtani leading their respective teams in home runs once again this year.

On the other hand, no one had Dillon Dingler as the Detroit Tigers top power threat on their preseason bingo card.

With that wide range of outcomes on full display during the 2026 MLB season, we've ranked every team's current home run leader on surprise level relative to preseason expectations.

Before we dive into the rankings, here's a list of the projected preseason leader for each team, based on the Depth Charts projection system from FanGraphs :

ARI: Corbin Carroll/Ketel Marte, 27 ATH: Nick Kurtz, 36 ATL: Ronald Acuña Jr./Matt Olson, 31 BAL: Pete Alonso, 37 BOS: Willson Contreras, 23 CHC: Michael Busch, 28 CWS: Munetaka Murakami, 29 CIN: Eugenio Suárez, 36 CLE: José Ramírez, 29 COL: Hunter Goodman, 29 DET: Riley Greene, 29 HOU: Yordan Alvarez, 30 KC: Bobby Witt Jr., 29 LAA: Jo Adell, 34 LAD: Shohei Ohtani, 46 MIA: Kyle Stowers, 21 MIL: Jackson Chourio, 25 MIN: Byron Buxton, 30 NYM: Juan Soto, 37 NYY: Aaron Judge, 44 PHI: Kyle Schwarber, 43 PIT: Oneil Cruz, 24 SD: Fernando Tatis Jr., 31 SF: Rafael Devers, 31 SEA: Cal Raleigh, 40 STL: Nolan Gorman, 24 TB: Junior Caminero, 39 TEX: Jake Burger, 30 TOR: Vladimir Guerrero Jr., 32 WAS: James Wood, 28

30. Kyle Schwarber, PHI — 37 HR 29. Shohei Ohtani, LAD — 30 HR 28. Junior Caminero, TB — 35 HR 27. Pete Alonso, BAL — 29 HR 26. Hunter Goodman, COL — 34 HR 25. James Wood, WAS — 30 HR 24. Yordan Alvarez, HOU — 36 HR 23. Juan Soto, NYM — 21 HR 22. Matt Olson, ATL — 36 HR 21. Rafael Devers, SF — 25 HR

With the exception of Pete Alonso who was still on the Mets, Yordan Alvarez who played in only 48 games and Rafael Devers who joined the Giants in a midseason trade, all of the players listed above led their club in home runs last year.

Most are well-established, middle-of-the-order sluggers, and even Hunter Goodman and James Wood had a 30-homer campaign in 2025 to help solidify their status.

The real surprise would be if anyone from this group failed to lead their team in long balls, and it likely would have taken an injury for that to happen.

20. Byron Buxton, MIN — 25 HR 19. Ketel Marte, ARI — 21 HR 18. Manny Machado, SD — 24 HR 17. Brandon Lowe, PIT — 27 HR 16. Shea Langeliers, ATH — 23 HR 15. Pete Crow-Armstrong, CHC — 31 HR 14. Zach Neto, LAA — 21 HR 13. Willson Contreras, BOS — 25 HR

The only thing keeping Byron Buxton off the "No Brainers" page is his injury history, but with 25 home runs in 88 games he edges out Kody Clemens (21 HR) for the team lead.

Ketel Marte , Manny Machado , Brandon Lowe , Shea Langeliers and Pete Crow-Armstrong all entered 2026 with 30-homer seasons on their resume, but power-hitting teammates capable of edging them out for the team lead were enough to land them with this second group.

The Angels leaderboard is a two-man race between Zach Neto (21 HR) and Mike Trout (20 HR) right now, and with Jo Adell traded to the Guardians, they are now the logical top sluggers on the roster.

The Red Sox did not have a major power threat on the roster last season, with Trevor Story pacing the club with 25 homers. Offseason pickup Willson Contreras was projected to lead the team heading into the year, but his 25 bombs also represent a career-high, so he was far from a no-brainer.

12. Munetaka Murakami, CWS — 29 HR 11. Jac Caglianone, KC — 22 HR 10. Sal Stewart, CIN — 27 HR 9. Kazuma Okamoto, TOR — 26 HR

Munetaka Murakami and Kazuma Okamoto both produced prolific power numbers in Japan, but it's never a given that production will translate immediately.

Murakami being the face of the White Sox resurgence is not the biggest shock given his track record and the young roster around him, but Okamoto outpacing Vladimir Guerrero Jr., George Springer and others has been a bright spot in a disappointing year for the Blue Jays.

Jac Caglianone entered pro ball with some of the best raw power of any prospect after a storied collegiate career at Florida, and while he was slow to adjust to the big league game after debuting last year, he is starting to come into his own.

With perennial 30/30 threat Elly De La Cruz and veteran slugger Eugenio Suarez on the roster, Sal Stewart leading the Reds roster and all NL rookies with 27 homers has been a nice boon to the organization's future outlook. He gave a glimpse of his pop a year ago with five homers in 18 games as a September call-up.

After slugging 26 home runs in his first full season in the majors in 2025, Rice taking another step forward with his first 30-homer campaign has not been a major shock.

However, Aaron Judge was the obvious candidate to lead the team in long balls before he was injured, and Trent Grisham, Jazz Chisholm Jr. and Cody Bellinger also out-homered Rice a year ago, so his leapfrog to the top of the team leaderboard qualifies as a legitimate surprise.

The Rangers signed Joc Pederson to a two-year, $37 million deal prior to the 2025 season, and he was a major flop in his first season with the team, hitting .181 with nine home runs in 306 plate appearances.

The 34-year-old has bounced back nicely this season, and with Corey Seager and Wyatt Langford both missing time to injury, his 22 bombs have been enough to pace a Rangers team vying for the AL West title.

After hitting a combined .211/.270/.324 with 11 home runs and a 30.7 percent strikeout rate in 574 plate appearances between the 2024 and 2025 seasons, Jordan Walker was tiptoeing dangerously close to bust territory entering 2026.

The former first-round pick and top prospect has finally turned a corner this season, delivering on the elite-level power potential he showed throughout his time in the minors.

No. 5 Biggest Surprise: Heriberto Hernández, Miami Marlins

Considering Kyle Stowers was the only player on the Marlins roster projected to hit more than 20 home runs with a whopping 21, the placement here is as much team-centric as it is player-centric.

That said, how many people outside of Miami knew who Heriberto Hernández was at the start of the year?

The 26-year-old joined the Marlins as a minor league free agent prior to the 2025 season, and he quietly debuted with a 118 OPS+ and 10 home runs in 87 games a year ago. He is a bat-only player with limited value beyond what he does in the batter's box, but he has turned into a viable run producer.

No. 4 Biggest Surprise: Julio Rodríguez/Dominic Canzone, Seattle Mariners

Cal Raleigh was baseball's biggest breakout star during the 2025 season, launching 60 home runs to set a new single-season record for a catcher while finishing runner-up to Aaron Judge in AL MVP voting.

Anyone other than him leading the team in homers this year would have been a shocking prediction heading into the year, but his production has fallen off a cliff, as he sports a .156 average and 13 home runs in 94 games.

Julio Rodríguez was the obvious candidate to pace the team if it wasn't Raleigh, but him sharing the lead with Dominic Canzone is an unexpected turn of events.

The Mariners have lacked consistent middle-of-the-order thump all year, and it's the biggest hole on a team with a rock-solid starting staff.

No. 3 Biggest Surprise: Chase DeLauter/Rhys Hoskins/Kyle Manzardo, Cleveland Guardians

That's not a typo: 13 home runs is enough to lead the Guardians.

Few clubs had a more obvious home run leader entering the year than Cleveland, with star third baseman José Ramírez coming off a 30-homer campaign and yet another top-five finish in AL MVP balloting.

However, a slow start followed by a fractured hamate bone in June has sapped his power and cost him time, and that created a major power void throughout the Guardians lineup.

Rookie Chase DeLauter hit four home runs in his first three games to open the year, which has helped prop up his total. Veterans Rhys Hoskins and Kyle Manzardo have both been viable 30-homer threats in the past, but the real shock here is that it's not J-Ram and it's not more than 13.

No. 2 Biggest Surprise: Dillon Dingler, Detroit Tigers

Dillon Dingler seized Detroit's starting catcher job last season with a 3.2-WAR campaign, and while he posted a 108 OPS+ with 13 home runs, much of that value was built on his defense as he was the AL Gold Glove winner at catcher.

Riley Greene (36 HR in 2025), Spencer Torkelson (31 HR in 2025) and Kerry Carpenter (26 HR in 2025) were all logical candidates to lead the Tigers in homers, but Dingler was projected for just 13 long balls once again.

Instead, he has already doubled his previous total, and with an expected slugging percentage that ranks in the 90th percentile it looks like a sustainable spike in power production.

With club control through 2030 and the foundation of his elite defense, Dingler has quickly emerged as one of the most valuable players on the Detroit roster and a legitimate middle-of-the-order run producer.

No. 1 Biggest Surprise: Jake Bauers, Milwaukee Brewers

Jake Bauers was a cheap power source for the Brewers in 2024 and 2025, but the club's small-market profile made him a non-tender candidate at the start of last offseason.

Instead, he returned on a $2.7 million salary in his second year of arbitration, and that has made him one of the biggest bargains of the year as he has been an anchor in the middle of the lineup for the first-place Brewers.

The 30-year-old had never topped 12 home runs in a season prior to this year, and preseason projections had him eighth on the club with 12 homers and only 294 plate appearances.

Rather than filling a part-time role, he has a 144 OPS+ with 22 home runs and 72 RBI over 461 plate appearances while spending much of the year penciled into the No. 3 and No. 4 spots in the batting order.

articles.title: Dodgers President Addresses Sale Rumors After Mark Walter Sells Lakers for Record $12.5B
articles.summary: In the wake of Mark Walter's surprise decision to sell the Los Angeles Lakers, there doesn't appear to be any indication within the Los Angeles Dodgers organization that they are going to change owners.
articles.body:
In the wake of Mark Walter's surprise decision to sell the Los Angeles Lakers, there doesn't appear to be any indication within the Los Angeles Dodgers organization that they are going to change owners.

Dodgers president Stan Kasten dismissed any rumors of a sale when asked about the situation on Friday.

"The Dodgers are not being sold. They're not for sale. There's no process that has been started to sell it, period," Kasten told reporters . "We are planning only to win."

Kasten went on to explain that Walter views the Dodgers differently than he did the Lakers.

"I can't tell you how important the Dodgers are to Mark," Kasten said. "The Lakers thing? The Lakers were important to him too, but it's kind of an extraordinary opportunity, which he took."

Walter, whose purchase of the Lakers was approved by the NBA board of governors in October 2025, agreed to sell the franchise at a record $12.5 billion valuation to Bob Iger and Joshua Kushner on Aug. 12.

Given the lack of any hint the Lakers were even on the market, there was immediate speculation about the possibility of the Dodgers being available.

Kasten previously said the Lakers' sale was "not really a Dodgers story" because they are "completely separate" and there were "no changes" to what the MLB club was doing.

A Dodgers sale could have huge ramifications on MLB beyond who is in charge of the franchise. Shohei Ohtani negotiated into his contract a "key man" clause that allows him to opt out if Walter or president of baseball operations Andrew Friedman were to leave the organization.

Per The Athletic's Sam Blum and Stephen J. Nesbitt , Ohtani would be "unlikely" to use his opt-out if it came into play. He is under contract through the 2033 season, though he will be owed $680 million in deferred money that gets paid out over 10 years starting in 2034.

Walter has been the controlling owner of the Dodgers since 2012. He was part of the Guggenheim Baseball Management group that purchased the club from Frank McCourt for $2.15 billion , a record sale price at the time for an MLB franchise.

The Dodgers have made the playoffs every year during Walter's tenure as controlling owner. They have won three World Series titles in five appearances, including each of the last two years.

If the Dodgers win a World Series again this season, they will become the first team to three-peat since the New York Yankees from 1998-2000.

articles.title: Andy Pages Injured by HPB, Latest on Dodgers Star After Concern of Season-Ending Fracture in Hand
articles.summary: The Los Angeles Dodgers' mood after a 5-4 win over the Pittsburgh Pirates on Friday was tempered by the news that Andy Pages suffered a fracture on the back of his left hand after being hit by a pitch.
articles.body:
The Los Angeles Dodgers' mood after a 5-4 win over the Pittsburgh Pirates on Friday was tempered by the news that Andy Pages suffered a fracture on the back of his left hand after being hit by a pitch.

Dodgers manager Dave Roberts revealed the news of Pages' injury after the game, but the expectation is he won't miss the rest of the season.

"It's not season-ending because obviously things like that it's four or five weeks," Roberts told reporters . "I would expect him back, knowing him, on the earlier side. There's still time in the season for him to be back. I feel for him because he's having such a good year."

Pages was hit on the back of his hand by a pitch clocked at 100 mph from Pirates starter Bubba Chandler in the bottom of the third inning.

Roberts did note there's a possibility Pages could require surgery, but it's not believed that would change his return timeline.

Pages actually stayed in the game through the fourth inning before Enrique Hernández replaced him in center to start the top of the fifth.

A four-week timeline would have Pages back for the final week of the regular season. The Dodgers' nine-game lead in the NL West gives them the ability to avoid feeling like they have to rush him back, but they could look to get him some at-bats in games before the playoffs if he is healthy.

The regular season ends on Sept. 27. If the Dodgers finish as one of the top two seeds in the NL, they wouldn't play until Oct. 3 when the Division Series begins.

Los Angeles currently has a three game lead over the Atlanta Braves for the No. 2 seed in the National League. The Dodgers are only two games behind the Milwaukee Brewers for the best record in MLB, but Milwaukee holds the tiebreaker thanks to a 4-3 head-to-head record.

The news about Pages comes as the Dodgers are uncertain about Dalton Rushing's status for the rest of the regular season due to a partially torn UCL.

Rushing did say this week he is progressing to be able to throw with the hope he can catch again at some point in September.

Pages' injury also interrupts what has been a terrific season for him. The 25-year-old is hitting .272/.338/.458 with 21 homers in 128 games. He is also an elite defensive centerfielder with 17 defensive runs saved, second-most at the position behind Ceddanne Rafaela (19).

Hernández and Tommy Edman will likely receive the bulk of the playing time in center until Pages can return.

articles.title: Josh Naylor's Must-See Iced-Out 'Space Jam' Jordan 11 Cleats Go Viral in Trending MLB Video
articles.summary: Seattle Mariners first baseman Josh Naylor went above and beyond with his look to kickoff MLB Players' Weekend on Friday night.
articles.body:
Seattle Mariners first baseman Josh Naylor went above and beyond with his look to kickoff MLB Players' Weekend on Friday night.

During the Mariners' game against the Chicago Cubs, Naylor was wearing a pair of iced-out Space Jam Jordan 11 cleats.

Naylor has an affinity for the 1996 Michael Jordan film, including comparing the New York Yankees to the Monstars in 2023 when he was playing for the Cleveland Guardians.

The Space Jam cleats were one of several unique items showcased by players around MLB on Friday night. Naylor's teammate Julio Rodríguez used a custom Spider-Man bat, for example.

MLB adopted Players' Weekend in 2017 to allow players to show off more of their personality by relaxing usual requirements for on-field equipment and attire.

Naylor's cleats and Rodríguez's bat must have helped since the Mariners defeated the Cubs 6-5 on Leo Rivas' walk-off single in the bottom of the 10th.

articles.title: Ketel Marte Casino Photos, Video Addressed by Diamondbacks Manager Torey Lovullo
articles.summary: On the heels of not showing up to Fenway Park for Monday's game against the Boston Red Sox and subsequently being placed on the injured list, Ketel Marte became a topic of conversation again on Friday night when he was spotted at a casino while the Arizona Diamondbacks were playing.
articles.body:
On the heels of not showing up to Fenway Park for Monday's game against the Boston Red Sox and subsequently being placed on the injured list, Ketel Marte became a topic of conversation again on Friday night when he was spotted at a casino while the Arizona Diamondbacks were playing.

After a 9-0 win over the Cincinnati Reds, Diamondbacks manager Torey Lovullo told reporters he wasn't aware of Marte's whereabouts, then explained that he was "free to do whatever he wants" as long as he is doing the required rehab work while on the IL.

Videos and images were posted on social media showing Marte at Talking Stick Resort in Scottsdale.

Salt River Fields is the spring training home to the Diamondbacks and where injured D-Backs rehab during the season. It's located three miles from Talking Stick Resort.

Marte was initially placed on the restricted list for not showing up to Monday's game.

Nick Piecoro of the Arizona Republic reported late Monday after the game was over that Marte was flying back to Arizona to undergo an MRI on his knee.

Marte was moved to the IL on Thursday after a meeting with him, his agent, Lovullo and D-Backs general manager Mike Hazen.

Details of the meeting were not made public beyond Hazen calling it "productive."

Speaking to reporters prior to Friday's game against the Reds, Lovullo admitted he felt "betrayed" when asked to describe his reaction to Marte's initial absence.

"Once I saw what was unfolding, I became extremely frustrated. I felt betrayed," Lovullo said. "And that's a whole different type of pain and frustration. But I'm through that."

Lovullo didn't have a definite answer when asked what he thought caused Marte to no-show, though he did suggest there was "maybe a little bit of frustration" from his knee injury and "a few things that I want to keep personal" they were trying to work through with him.

Despite missing games earlier in the season due to a back issue, Marte avoided an IL stint until this week. He is in the midst of his worst season since 2022 with a .249/.314/.446 slash line and 21 homers in 118 games.

Marte made the All-Star team in each of the previous two years and finished third in NL MVP voting in 2024.

Arizona (68-61) is one game behind the San Diego Padres in the race for the No. 3 wild card spot in the NL.

articles.title: Giancarlo Stanton Injured Falling While Running, Latest on Yankees Star amid Season-Ending Concern
articles.summary: New York Yankees designated hitter Giancarlo Stanton has been limited to 24 games this season due to injury, and now his 2026 campaign may be over.
articles.body:
New York Yankees designated hitter Giancarlo Stanton has been limited to 24 games this season due to injury, and now his 2026 campaign may be over.

Yankees manager Aaron Boone told reporters Saturday that Stanton may be out for the rest of the season after he suffered a moderate calf strain as a result of a fall while running.

Stanton was originally placed on the injured list in late April because of a calf strain. He suffered a setback in June, which extended his IL stint, and now the 36-year-old veteran has strained his other calf.

Little League World Series star Kinley Rasmus' MLB family

Prior to his injury, Stanton was off to a solid start at the plate, slashing .256/.302/.422 with three home runs and 14 RBI in just 24 contests.

Stanton had smacked at least 24 home runs in each of the previous five campaigns with the Yanks despite appearing in 114 or fewer games in four of those seasons.

Last season, elbow injuries limited Stanton to only 77 regular-season games, but the powerful slugger was highly productive in those appearances, slashing .273/.350/.594 with 24 homers and 66 RBI.

Stanton is relatively one-dimensional at this point in his career, as he is a liability on the bases and hasn't played more than 38 games in the outfield since 2018, which was his first year in New York.

Where Stanton's presence could truly be missed, though, is the playoffs, as he has been a strong postseason performer throughout his time with the Yankees.

Playing in 48 playoff games for the Bronx Bombers since 2018, Stanton has slashed .254/.322/.605 with 18 home runs and 44 RBI.

Much of that damage was done en route to a World Series appearance in 2024 when Stanton slashed .273/.339/.709 with seven home runs and 16 RBI in 14 postseason games.

He crushed four homers and drove in seven during the 2024 American League Championship Series against the Cleveland Guardians' earning him ALCS MVP honors.

A five-time All-Star, two-time Silver Slugger Award winner and one-time National League MVP, Stanton is one of the top power hitters of his era with 456 home runs and 1,183 RBI in his career.

While the Yankees undoubtedly would have loved to have his power and clutch hitting in the playoffs, they do possess the depth to make up for it if the rest of their lineup is largely healthy.

Outfielder Cody Bellinger is expected to return from the IL on Sunday, and while superstar slugger Aaron Judge has been on the IL since June with a rib injury, he continues to make progress, and the expectation remains that he will return this season.

On top of that, the Yankees added Luis García Jr. and Heliot Ramos at the trade deadline, youngsters George Lombard Jr. and Spencer Jones are cementing their spots on the team, and the likes of Ben Rice and Trent Grisham are playing key roles as well.

New York also boasts arguably the best starting rotation in baseball with Cam Schlittler, Gerrit Cole, Max Fried and Carlos Rodón, arguably making it the team to beat in the American League, along with the Tampa Bay Rays, who lead the Yankees by three games for the best record in the AL.
